This function is particularly useful for obtaining pricing, specifications, and availability details when you have a valid Amazon product ID (ASIN). The product ID can be found in Amazon's product URLs following the '/dp/' segment, e.g., 'B08N5WG761' in 'https://www.amazon.in/.../dp/B08N5WG761/...' Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

productid.description: The Amazon product identifier (ASIN) used to look up the product. This 10-character alphanumeric string is typically found in Amazon's product URLs following the '/dp/' path segment.

functions.name: get_a_product_details

productid.description: The Amazon product identifier (ASIN) used to look up the product. This 10-character alphanumeric string is typically found in Amazon's product URLs following the '/dp/' path segment.

messages.content: I need to source affordable art supplies for a community workshop I'm organizing. Let's start with this link to a Canson watercolor paper pad on Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/Canson-Watercolor-Paper-11-Inch-9-Inch/dp/B001GZ6QXC. Can you first check its current price and availability? Then, based on the paper size and weight (140lb/300gsm), find similar products from other brands like Arches or Strathmore that might offer better bulk pricing for 10+ pads? Finally, can you cross-reference these options with any available Amazon coupons or educator discounts that might apply? I'd love to stretch our budget as far as possible.

functions.name: store_locator
functions.description: Retrieves store locations based on search criteria such as location, category, or proximity. Returns store details including address, operating hours, and contact information. Ideal for helping customers find nearby physical stores with customizable filters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: Search location specified as a human-readable address or geographic coordinates (e.g., 'Los Angeles, CA' or '34.0522,-118.2437'). Required for proximity-based searches.

radius.description: Search radius in kilometers from the specified location. Must be between 1 and 500 km.

search_term.description: Text to partially match store names, addresses, or descriptions. Returns all stores when omitted.

category.description: Filter stores by category (e.g., 'electronics', 'fashion', 'grocery'). Leave empty to include all categories.

limit.description: Maximum number of store results to return. Minimum 1, maximum 20.

include_all_details.description: Whether to return full store details including operating hours, contact info, and inventory availability. Defaults to returning basic location data.

latitude.description: Geographic latitude coordinate in decimal degrees format. Must be an integer value within the range [-90, 90].

functions.name: business_days_work_days_calculator_api
functions.description: Calculates the date after a specified number of workdays, considering weekends and holidays based on the country's calendar. This function is useful for business date calculations where accurate workday tracking (including regional holidays) is required. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_date.description: The starting date for calculations in DD/MM/YYYY format. This date is included in the workday count if it falls on a workday.

work_days.description: Number of workdays to add to the start date. Must be a positive integer representing the duration to calculate.

state.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US' for United States, 'GB' for United Kingdom) used to determine region-specific holidays and weekend rules.

options.description: Defines which days to skip during calculation. 0 skips both holidays and weekends (default), 1 skips weekends only, 2 skips holidays only.

mode.description: Routing mode selection that determines path calculation strategy. Choose based on vehicle/travel type.

functions.name: next_charging_station
functions.description: Finds electric vehicle charging stations within a specified geographic bounding box. Returns results based on search density level with a maximum of 2000 stations per request. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

latmax.description: Maximum latitude of the bounding box area to search within (in decimal degrees). Must be between -90 and 90.

latmin.description: Minimum latitude of the bounding box area to search within (in decimal degrees). Must be between -90 and 90.

densitylevel.description: Density level for charging station search, determining the granularity of results. Valid values: 3 (lowest density) to 15 (highest density).

lngmax.description: Maximum longitude of the bounding box area to search within (in decimal degrees). Must be between -180 and 180.

lngmin.description: Minimum longitude of the bounding box area to search within (in decimal degrees). Must be between -180 and 180.

functions.name: api_product

refinementid.description: Identifier for a specific product refinement option (e.g., brand, price range, or attribute filter). Use values returned by Amazon's refinement endpoints.

Use this function when you need weather insights for planning, analysis, or reporting purposes. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The geographic location to query, specified as a city and state, country name, or latitude/longitude coordinates (e.g., 'London, UK', 'Sydney', or '37.7749,-122.4194')

units.description: Temperature unit for the response data

days.description: Number of forecast days to return (1-14 days). Set to 0 for current conditions only.

include_hourly.description: Whether to include hourly forecast data in addition to daily summaries when forecast days are requested

functions.name: store_locator
functions.description: Retrieves store locations based on search criteria such as location, category, or proximity. Returns store details including address, operating hours, and contact information. Ideal for helping customers find nearby physical stores with customizable filters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: Search location specified as a human-readable address or geographic coordinates (e.g., 'Los Angeles, CA' or '34.0522,-118.2437'). Required for proximity-based searches.

radius.description: Search radius in kilometers from the specified location. Must be between 1 and 500 km.

search_term.description: Text to partially match store names, addresses, or descriptions. Returns all stores when omitted.

category.description: Filter stores by category (e.g., 'electronics', 'fashion', 'grocery'). Leave empty to include all categories.

limit.description: Maximum number of store results to return. Minimum 1, maximum 20.

include_all_details.description: Whether to return full store details including operating hours, contact info, and inventory availability. Defaults to returning basic location data.

functions.name: list_devices
functions.description: Retrieves a list of devices with optional filtering and pagination capabilities. Returns device identifiers, statuses, and configuration metadata for inventory management or monitoring purposes. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

device_type.description: Device category to filter results by. Valid values include 'router', 'sensor', 'server', and 'gateway'

status.description: Operational status filter. Valid states are 'active', 'inactive', 'maintenance', or 'decommissioned'

page.description: Page number for paginated results (1-based index)

page_size.description: Number of results per page (minimum 5, maximum 100)

include_metadata.description: Whether to include extended configuration details in the response

functions.name: searchairports
functions.description: Searches for airports based on a keyword match against airport names, city names, or codes (IATA, ICAO, city codes). Returns detailed airport information including coordinates, timezone, country details, and codes. Supports case-insensitive matching and configurable sorting/pagination. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

matchingkeywordairportorcityorcode.description: Search term to find airports by full or partial name, city name, or airport/city codes (IATA, ICAO, or UN/LOCODE). Case-insensitive matching is automatically applied.

sortby.description: Specifies sorting criteria in 'field:order' format (e.g., 'AirportName:asc', 'CityCode:desc'). Supported fields include AirportName, CityCode, CountryCode, and IATACode.

page.description: Pagination page number (1-based index). Used to navigate through large result sets.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page (1-20). Higher values may increase response time.

functions.name: retorna_os_registros_dos_ltimos_dias
functions.description: Retrieves historical exchange rate records for a specified currency pair over a defined number of recent days. Returns data in the requested response format (JSON, JSONP, or XML). Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

format.description: Response format type. Valid values: json, jsonp, xml

numero_dias.description: Number of recent days to return records for. Must be a numeric string. Default: '30' if not specified

moeda.description: Currency pair in {source}-{target} format (e.g., USD-BRL, EUR-BRL). Must be a supported exchange pair

functions.name: retrieving_past_content
functions.description: Retrieves historical entries from one or more feeds that the user is subscribed to. Returns entries in various formats including JSON or JSONP. This endpoint enables filtering by time range, pagination, and format customization. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

accept.description: Specifies the preferred response content type. Use 'application/json' for JSON-formatted feed entries (feeds only).

hub_topic.description: The URL of the feed resource to retrieve historical entries for. Must be a feed the user is currently subscribed to.

hub_callback.description: Either a specific callback URL identifying a subscription, or a search query matching one or more callback URLs. Limited to 200 matching feeds.

count.description: Maximum number of entries to return (1-50).

before.description: Entry ID boundary for filtering results. Returns only entries published before this specified entry ID.

after.description: Entry ID boundary for filtering results. Returns only entries published after this specified entry ID.

format.description: Response format override. Use 'json' for JSON-formatted feed entries (feeds only).

callback.description: JSONP callback function name. When provided, responses will be rendered using JSONP format.

functions.name: property_rent_estimate
functions.description: Returns a rent estimate and comparable rental listings for a specified property. Providing detailed property features improves estimate accuracy. Users must supply either a full address or latitude/longitude coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

bathrooms.description: Number of bathrooms (supports fractional values for partial bathrooms, e.g., 1.5 for one full and one half bathroom)

daysold.description: Maximum number of days since comparable listings were last active (minimum value: 1)

bedrooms.description: Total number of bedrooms in the property

maxradius.description: Maximum search radius in kilometers for comparable listings

squarefootage.description: Total living area size in square feet

latitude.description: Property latitude coordinate (use with longitude instead of address)

longitude.description: Property longitude coordinate (use with latitude instead of address)

address.description: Property address in 'Street, City, State, Zip' format (alternatively use latitude/longitude)

compcount.description: Number of comparable listings to return (valid range: 5-25)

normalized_functions.name: similar
normalized_functions.description: Returns a list of companies similar to the one specified by the provided domain. The response includes comprehensive information about the queried company ('frontend_company_info') and similarity scores for each comparable company. If additional data requires extended processing, the 'further_crawling' flag will indicate that enhanced results are available within 10-15 seconds. Querying the same domain multiple times consumes only a single search credit. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

domain.description: Company domain or full URL to analyze (e.g., 'unilever.com' or 'https://www.unilever.com'). The API will automatically extract and validate the root domain for processing.

limit.description: Maximum number of similar companies to return in the response (between 1 and 50, inclusive). Lower values improve response time. Additional results beyond this limit are included in the 'next_companies' field with basic domain and similarity percentage information.

q.description: The location query (e.g., city name, latitude/longitude).

tp.description: Time period for the weather forecast (e.g., '3 hourly'). Default is None.

lang.description: The language code for the weather forecast (default is 'en' for English).

format.description: The response format, such as 'json' or 'xml'. Default is None.

num_of_days.description: The number of days for the weather forecast, with a maximum of 7 days. Default is 1.

per_page.description: Maximum number of messages to return per page (cannot exceed 50)

messages.content: I need you to validate our new aircraft maintenance tracking API integration with the following workflow: 1. First, test the `/api/v1/maintenance/schedule` endpoint using our test environment credentials (API key: `XK89-test-mechanic`). 2. If the endpoint returns a 404 error, adjust the URL path to `/api/v1/aircraft/schedule` and retest. 3. Once the endpoint responds successfully, validate that the JSON response includes both `engine_serial` and `last_inspection_date` fields. 4. If either field is missing, run a schema comparison against our production API documentation (available at `https://docs.airport-tech.net/api/v1/schema`). 5. Finally, generate a compliance report comparing today's test results with last month's maintenance logs stored in our S3 bucket (`s3://airport-logs-2024/`). This needs to be completed by 5 PM PST so I can brief the FAA inspector tomorrow. Let me know immediately if you encounter authentication issues with the test environment.
